(i) there is no single programming abstraction that can be applied to all distributed graph processing problems; (ii) the choice of a programming abstraction is highly dependent on the problem at hand; and (iii) there is a lack of a unified graph processing model that can be used by all distributed graph processing systems, and that can be used as a basis to develop a unified graph processing system.

the most prevalent graph processing models are: (1) Pregel, which is a graph-centric programming abstraction for iterative refinement, (2) GraphX, a graph processing abstraction for iterative refinement and graph transformations, and (3) Pregel++, an extension of Pregel with graph pattern matching.
